subject: POC observability: success criteria, dashboards, and timeline
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.li@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Torres <diego@averylabs.com>, security@averylabs.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC observability recap and proposed next steps

Hi Diego — great call earlier today, thanks for walking us through your ML infra and goals. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture a concise recap and proposed plan so we stay aligned as we kick off the 3-week POC.

High-level goal
- Validate Redwood Dedicated will meet Avery Labs' latency and cost targets for LLM-powered search and chat across 2 regions (us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 failover).

Primary success criteria (you asked for measurable outcomes):
1) 95th percentile generator latency <= 200ms for top-priority route at 512 tokens (realistic production traffic shape).
2) End-to-end token cost reduction vs current baseline by >= 35% using batching + KV caching over a 7-day run.
3) No data exfiltration — logs/metrics exported to your SIEM (S3 + CloudWatch subscription) only; model inputs not persisted in hosting logs.
4) Dashboarding: per-route latency, token-cost-per-request, error rate, and KV cache hit ratio available in our Console within first 5 business days.

POC timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (this week): onboarding access + infra checklist completed (you + procurement).
- Week 1: baseline traffic replay + restore-model validation; Console dashboard skeleton live.
- Week 2: performance tuning (batching/quantization recommendations) and tracing enabled; run 48–72h stress window.
- Week 3: final validation, handoff, and measurement report.

Ownership
- Redwood (Jasmine): POC project lead, Console dashboard setup, perf tuning recommendations, final report.
- Avery (Diego): provide traffic replay export, grant access to test VPC endpoint, and confirm compliance requirements with your security team.

Attachments: rwd_poc_observability_checklist.xlsx (POC checklist), a short infra requirements PDF attached for procurement.

Next steps
1) Diego: share a sanitized traffic replay (s3 link) and confirm procurement contact for onboarding OTP by EOD Monday.
2) Avery security: confirm allowed log export destinations (S3 bucket ARN) and whether KMS must be customer-managed.
3) Redwood: provision a development capacity pool and post a Console invite to Lauren and Diego by Monday.

Thanks — I’ll follow up internally to confirm the detailed eval plan and assign owners.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC observability recap and proposed next steps

Thanks Jasmine — appreciated the clear summary. Quick clarifications from our side: 
- We can provide a 7-day traffic replay (sanitized, removes PII) by Tuesday morning. Will upload to s3://avery-poc-uploads and share the presigned link.
- Security: KMS must be customer-managed; logs must land in our S3 bucket and be lifecycle'd to 90 days.
- Procurement: procurement@averylabs.com will need the infra PDF and order form to start approval; I’ve looped them into this thread.

One ask: can Redwood expose a simple tracing span for token pipeline (frontend request -> model invoke -> KV cache hit/miss)? That’ll make it far easier for our infra team to map latency.

Diego
Head of Platform Engineering, Avery Labs

Subject: Internal: Avery POC – observability evaluation plan and task list

Team — following Diego's responses, draft eval plan and owners below. Please review and flag anything missing. I’ll send the external version once we confirm responsibilities.

POC objective (same as external): validate latency, cost, and secure log export for Avery Labs' workloads.

Success criteria (measurable):
- S1 (latency): 95th <= 200ms at 512 tokens for "search_route_v1" during the 48–72h validation window.
- S2 (cost): token-cost-per-response reduced >= 35% vs their supplied baseline traffic replay for the 7-day run.
- S3 (security): logs must be exported only to their S3 ARN and encrypted with their CMK; no full-text request bodies retained in our long-term logging.
- S4 (observability coverage): Console shows these panels by Day 5: per-route latency (p50/p90/p95), token cost per route, KV cache hit ratio, 500/4xx rates, and an end-to-end trace view that surfaces cache hits.

Concrete deliverables & owners:
- Provision dev capacity + test endpoint (Infra): LA/ops (Rishi) — due Tue EOD.
- Console dashboard scaffold and raw metrics pipeline (Observability): Jasmine — due Wed EOD.
- Tracing span for token pipeline (Runtime team): Rishi — instrument and expose spans with a standard header by Wed.
- Eval harness + baseline comparison notebook (Customer Evals): Lauren — prepare Jupyter + runbook by Thu.
- Security proofpoints (Compliance): Jasmine — gather audit log config and KMS notes; ask security@averylabs.com for bucket ARN asap.

Edge-case notes:
- If quantization reduces quality below their threshold, we should include a rollback to full-precision as part of the canary. Add eval prompts to detect regressions.
- If KV cache hit ratio is low (<10%), propose a short TTL tuning and re-run later.

Attachments: I uploaded the POC checklist to the shared Drive (link below). I also attached our internal template (rwd_poc_observability_checklist.xlsx).

Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/sales/avery-poc-observability

Please reply with any changes. I’ll consolidate and send the external version with dates.

-Jasmine
